ImageDescription.value:
In the Himalayas, in general the term Jhula is used to denote a hanging or cantilever bridge. The bridge shown here is at Rishikesh at the foothills of the Himalayas. It is named after Lord Rama. It is also known as SHIVANANDA Jhula or bridge.Incidentally, there is another similar hanging bridge over the Ganga few kilometres upstream, called LACHHMANJHULA (named after the younger brother of Lord Rama).

Previously such bridges were built of ropes, but now-a-days steel cables are in use.
Ramjhula - bridge over the Ganga

ImageDescription.value: Articles of incorporation of the Pacific Coast Khalsa Diwan (Free Divine Communion) Society, Department of State, State of California, 27 May 1912 (chapter no. 69371). Teja Singh is noted as the president with Tara Singh as the secretary. On 29 May 1912, Gurdwara Sahib Stockton was officially incorporated by early Sikh immigrants. The Stockton Gurdwara served as a religious, social, political, and educational hub for all South Asian pioneers throughout the early 20th century.

Artist.value: Benjamin Haydon

ImageDescription.value:
The Anti-Slavery Society Convention, 1840, by Benjamin Robert Haydon (died 1846), given to the National Portrait Gallery, London in 1880 by the British and Foreign Anti-Slavery Society. Oil on canvas, 1841. 117 in. x 151 in. (2972 mm x 3836 mm). See source website for additional information.

Quote from the description at the National Portrait Gallery website:

This monumental painting records the 1840 convention of the British and Foreign Anti-Slavery Society which was established to promote worldwide abolition. A frail and elderly [Thomas] Clarkson addresses a meeting of over 500 delegates. [...] Haydon later wrote: 'a liberated slave, now a delegate, is looking up to Clarkson with deep interest ... this is the point of interest in the picture, and illustrative of the object in painting it, the African sitting by the intellectual European, in equality and intelligence'.
